title: Evidence Types and Inference Validity
purpose: Seed typed evidence and evidence-to-claim validity so Lantern distinguishes what was observed, measured, reported, documented, experimentally manipulated, simulated or inferred, and asks whether an evidence item can actually support the claim being evaluated.

concepts.definition: Information used to increase, decrease or constrain support for a claim under an explicit inferential relationship.
Evidence is relevant when its truth/quality would change rational support for the claim under consideration.
A recorded observation of an event/state by an observer or sensor, still subject to perspective, detection and recording limits.
An observation produced by an instrument/procedure mapping a property to a value under defined units and uncertainty.
A person's or agent's report about what they observed, remember, infer or believe.
A preserved record whose evidential value depends on provenance, authenticity, context and relation to the claim.
Evidence produced by a designed intervention/comparison intended to distinguish hypotheses under controlled assumptions.
Evidence gathered without controlled assignment/intervention; useful for description/association but causal interpretation needs additional justification.
Results produced by a model/computation; evidence about consequences of the model and assumptions, not automatically direct evidence that reality matches them.
A conclusion derived from premises/evidence through a stated inference; its support depends on both inference validity and premise quality.
An expected observation is absent or contrary evidence appears under conditions where detection was adequate.
A small or unsystematically selected set of individual observations/reports; potentially informative but weak for broad frequency/generalization claims.
Evidence from sufficiently independent methods/sources that bears on the same claim.
Evidence items are independent to the degree they do not merely inherit the same underlying observation/source/error.
The conclusion follows from premises under the declared inference rule; validity is separate from premise truth/evidence quality.
A provenance-linked sequence from source/observation through transformations/inferences to a claim.

guards.reason: Testimony directly establishes that a source reported P, not that P is true.
A document preserves a claim; authenticity, provenance, context and reliability still matter.
Simulation output is conditional on model structure/inputs and is not direct observation.
The instrument/procedure must validly measure the intended property.
An anecdote does not establish prevalence or broad generalization.
Repetition through citation may be one evidence chain, not independent confirmation.
Copied/repackaged evidence does not replicate the underlying observation.
A valid argument can have false/unverified premises.
Evidence can be relevant while weak, noisy, biased or ambiguous.
Many dependent/low-quality items need not provide strong evidence.
Causal inference requires additional design/assumptions beyond association.
Missing evidence counts against H only if H predicted E and detection was adequate.

invariants: Evidence type and evidence quality are separate.
Evidence must be relevant to the claim before its strength matters.
Observation records what was observed; interpretation/inference is represented separately.
Measurement requires a defined mapping between instrument/procedure and target property.
Testimony/documentation preserves attribution and provenance rather than becoming fact automatically.
Simulation output is conditional evidence about a model/assumptions, not direct reality observation.
Formal inference validity and premise evidential quality are separate dimensions.
Independent convergence can strengthen evidence; repeated copies of one source do not count as independent confirmation.
Anecdotes can motivate hypotheses or establish existence in a case but do not establish population prevalence by themselves.
Observational association does not by itself establish causation.
Every derived evidential claim should retain a chain back to its supporting evidence/provenance.

provenance.authoring_basis: General epistemology of evidence, scientific evidence distinctions and formal inference validity, adapted to Lantern's provenance-first architecture.
